blockers: Signal Four Analytics (the source every FDOT manual requires) needs FDOT-approved access; no real S4 export seen, the reader is built from the public S4 Data Dictionary and the open MPO copies
No licence for paid use on FLHSMV Crash Facts or any open S4 copy
FLHSMV open file has no street names or report number: its ~25% no-GPS crashes can't be placed
Freeway/interchange crashes: street-pair placement is 4% within 250 ft; needs the freeway method with FDOT route geometry
No current public statewide average crash-rate table (FDOT computes district averages inside CAR/S4)
user_actions: Request S4 access through an FDOT project manager / District Safety office (AARF) and download one sample: Palm Beach County 2024 Event CSV (+ Driver/Passenger/Non-Motorist tables)
Ask FLHSMV Crash Statistics (850-617-3105) in writing whether the Crash Facts download may be displayed in a paid product
Ask Palm Beach MPO and MetroPlan Orlando whether their S4 layers may be used commercially
Decide: Florida as 'bring your S4 export' only, or also the open MPO copies for Palm Beach and the Orlando region

FDOT Safety Crash Data Guidance (Crash Data Process v18)
FDOT Manual on Uniform Traffic Studies (MUTS) 2027
TEO Bulletin 26-03 (2027 MUTS; ICE program retired)
FDOT Safety Office crash data FAQ (crash rate / confidence method)
FDOT Crash Data Academy CDA-9 High Crash Location Analysis for the SHS
FDOT Highway Safety Manual User Guide

methods.rates_unit: crashes per MVM (segments: ADT x miles x days / 1e6) and per MEV (intersections: ADT x days / 1e6); averages per district and rate category, computed inside CAR/S4, no current public table

crash_costs.year: FDM 2026 Table 122.6.2 (CAR 2015-2019 crashes, published 2022-02-23; dollar year not stated)

methods.screening_method: HSM peak searching on expected fatal+injury crash frequency (HSIP Guidelines 4.1.1); FDOT preference order: EB excess expected, SPF predicted, relative severity, critical rate (FDOT solves for K and reports a confidence level vs the district average), qualitative
methods.years_required: 5 full calendar years (MUTS 5.4.3.3 'shall' for EB; Crash Data Guidance); 3-5 years (HSIP)
differences_from_ca: Separate K and A costs (K $10.89M, A $888k) vs Caltrans LRSM combined KA by location type ($2.379M-$3.784M); FL PDO $7,700 vs CA $20,000
Average cost per crash by facility type (FDM Table 122.6.1) for relative-severity analysis; no CA equivalent in CrashIQ
Crash-rate test reports a confidence level vs the district category average (solve for K) instead of a fixed-K critical rate
No public statewide base-rate table like TASAS
EB excess expected crashes with Florida-calibrated SPFs is FDOT's preferred method
Signal Four is the required crash source; 5 full calendar years
FDOT forms: Condition Diagram 750-020-04, Collision Diagrams 750-020-05i/j, Collision Summary 750-020-05k
FDOT ICE program and manual retired effective 2026-11-02 (TEO Bulletin 26-03)
